newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica Brazil deal seen strategic.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica Brazil deal seen strategic.

text.p: Telefonica's entry into the Brazilian telecoms market is of high strategic value but initially the impact of the investment on the firm's earnings may be limited, Spanish analysts said on Wednesday.

Telefonica's foreign unit, Telefonica Internacional (TISA) was part of a consortium with Brazil's RBS Participacoes Industriales, Citicorp of the U.S., TISA affiliates Telefonica de Argentina and Chile's CTC which won the bidding to buy a 35 percent stake in Brazil's state telecoms operator Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT).
"It's positive news, more than for its impact on profits (it is positive) in terms of strategy" said Ignacio Cornejo, analyst at Beta Capital brokerage.
The news was well-received in Spain, dealers said, sending Telefonica's shares up yet more after a record run this year.
At 1430 GMT shares in Telefonica were up 35 pesetas, or 1.36 percent, to 2,975, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 1.9 percent to 4,827.45.
The TISA group offered 681 million reais for the stake ($655 million), just four million reais more than the next best offer from the group including Italy's STET.
"Brazil is the only country in Latin America where Telefonica wasn't present, and with this buy it's completed the process" said Jose Antonio Tamayo analyst at Inverban brokerage.
Brazil's telecoms market is not particularly developed, and so the growth potential there is high, Tamayo added.
An analyst at Agesban said the price paid for the stake was not at all unreasonable taking into account that the second offer was so close.
